title: TSMC's board approved up to $500 million each for Anthropic and OpenAI
friendlyTitle: TSMC's board approved up to $500 million each for Anthropic and OpenAI
summary: On 10 November, TSMC's board approved an investment of no more than US$500 million in Anthropic common shares, at Anthropic's IPO price, and no more than US$500 million in OpenAI preferred stock. The same meeting approved about US$40.9 billion in capital spending, mostly for advanced chip capacity, packaging, and fab construction, and a separate investment company capped at US$500 million.
friendlySummary: On 10 November, TSMC's board approved investments of no more than US$500 million in Anthropic and no more than US$500 million in OpenAI. The Anthropic shares would be bought at Anthropic's IPO price. The same meeting approved about US$40.9 billion to build and upgrade chip factories.
whyItMatters: This is an approval with a ceiling, not a confirmation that the money has been sent. It does put the main advanced-chip manufacturer on the cap table plans of both labs. For anyone buying AI tools, the nearer fact is the capacity spend: TSMC is still building the fabs those models depend on. The Anthropic line is tied to an IPO price, so it does not close until that offering does.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This is permission to invest, with a cap. It is not proof the money has already moved. The factory spending matters more for daily tools: these models still depend on TSMC's chips. The Anthropic investment waits for the IPO price.
